title: ‘Show How 3M Is 0% at Fault:’ Expert Witness Used ChatGPT to Write Report Defending Company in Deadly Explosion Lawsuit

reading.body:
This incident shows an expert witness using a general-purpose AI chatbot to produce a litigation document that is supposed to reflect independent professional judgment. The failure occurred at the point of report authorship: the witness prompted the system with a predetermined conclusion, asking it to show a specific party was zero percent at fault, and then submitted the output as expert testimony. That is a use case the system was not built for and one that inverts the proper function of expert analysis, which is to reach conclusions from evidence rather than to argue toward a conclusion supplied in advance.

The prompts became discoverable during litigation, which is how the practice came to light. Detection here did not require any technical audit of the AI output itself. It required only the ordinary legal mechanism of document discovery. The failure would have gone undetected had those prompts not been producible as case records.

What is not established is whether the court found the report inadmissible, whether 3M directed the witness to use the tool, or what consequence if any followed for the witness or the defense.

reports.title: ‘Show How 3M Is 0% at Fault:’ Expert Witness Used ChatGPT to Write Report Defending Company in Deadly Explosion Lawsuit

summary:
An expert witness hired by 3M to defend the company in a lawsuit over a deadly 2020 Houston explosion used ChatGPT to write significant portions of his expert report. Court documents revealed that the witness asked the AI chatbot to help him create a report showing how 3M was zero percent at fault for the incident at Watson Grinding, a manufacturing facility. The explosion killed three people and destroyed approximately 200 homes, resulting in a $61 million lawsuit with hundreds of millions in total liability at stake.

The case highlights how artificial intelligence is increasingly being used in legal proceedings, including expert witness testimony. A degraded rubber welding hose at the facility leaked flammable gas that eventually exploded, according to investigators. Multiple homeowners sued 3M and Watson Grinding, claiming 3M failed to properly maintain the facility's gas detection system and made other errors contributing to the disaster. The AI prompts used to generate the expert testimony became discoverable documents during the case, potentially damaging to the company's defense.
